newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels launch big attack on military.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels launch big attack on military.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels launched a major attack on Sri Lankan troops near the northern town of Vavuniya early on Tuesday, military officials in the north said.

They said the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels were attacking the military's forward defence line between Thandikulam and Nochchimoddai near Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
The Defence Ministry in Colombo confirmed the attack and said the rebels had been repelled.
"The attack was repulsed by troops causing large casualties among terrorists. The area that came under attack is being cleared presently," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
He said further details were awaited.

Residents in Vavuniya said the attack began at about 2.30 am (2030 GMT) and they could still hear artillery fire. They said artillery shells fired by the rebels had hit areas west of Vavuniya though the town itself was safe.
They said the road to Thandikulam had been sealed and some military casualties had been brought to Vavuniya.
Civilians, fleeing the shelling, were coming into Vavuniya from Thandikulam, 3.2 km (two miles) north of the town, they said.
Unofficial reports said at least 10 civilians had been wounded in the attack, but the number of military casualties was not immediately known.
Residents said they had seen Sri Lankan helicopter gunships and Kfir jets fly to the battle area to take on LTTE targets near Thandikulam.

The Sri Lankan military is in the midst of a nearly four-week-old major operation against the rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
Some 20,000 government troops are advancing on two flanks into the mostly shrub-covered rebel stronghold.
The army captured the towns of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya on one flank, and Nedunkeni, 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya on the other, in an offensive launched on May 13.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte said last week the offensive's aim was to open a land supply route to Jaffna, 100 km (60 miles) further north of Vavuniya, that would help rehabilitation work there.
The north-south highway has been closed for more than 10 years due to the war which began in 1983.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media have not been allowed into the war zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began. The rebels say the toll is higher.
